title: Microsoft Launches New AI PC with NVIDIA RTX Spark Chip: Starting at $2,600

content_html:
The integration of personal computers and artificial intelligence hardware is reaching a new milestone. This week, Microsoft officially revealed the specifications and pricing details of the new Surface Laptop Ultra notebook and the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box workstation at its technology week event in San Francisco, which features the NVIDIA RTX Spark chip.

In terms of product lineup and pricing, the new Surface Laptop Ultra offers two base models with starting prices of $2,600 and $3,700 respectively. Users can further upgrade memory and storage based on their needs, with the top configuration reaching up to $5,900. Microsoft mentioned that the highest-end model has already sold out since its release. Additionally, the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box workstation for professional developers starts at $6,000 and comes pre-installed with a full set of Microsoft development tools including VS Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, WSL, and PowerShell 7.

In terms of hardware design and local AI operation capabilities, the core highlights of these devices include the ability to run various AI models and agents directly on the device for free. Equipped with dedicated CPU, GPU, unified memory architecture, and an advanced cooling system optimized for high-load operations, the new models demonstrate strong local computing power. In addition to supporting AI and agent development, thanks to their powerful graphics processing performance, Microsoft promises that these Surface computers can also perfectly handle diverse scenarios such as content creation, video editing, and large-scale gaming.

On the operating system front, Microsoft simultaneously launched a fully redesigned Windows 11 and introduced a key feature called "Execution Containers" (execution containers). Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella pointed out during the event that this feature aims to provide a safer and more convenient sandboxed environment for AI agents, and this feature will be available to all Windows 11 users in the future. Nadella emphasized that relying solely on large models is not enough; the core of the future operating system lies in providing a collaborative layer that integrates multiple models, context, external memory, and operational space.

To attract developers, Microsoft launched a strong marketing strategy, offering a trade-in discount of up to $1,000 for MacBook Pro users exchanging their old devices. At the same time, other major PC manufacturers are also accelerating their layout. Dell officially announced the detailed specifications of the highly anticipated Dell XPS 16 Creator Edition PC on the same day, priced at $3,800 and now accepting pre-orders, with expected delivery in late October.
